summary: Turn evidence into accessible digital stories, reusable knowledge, and policy briefs. Explore the five-day intermediate course.
lede: Evidence-based digital communication helps communications, knowledge-management, and policy professionals turn research, data, and practitioner knowledge into useful content and advice. The training covers appraising evidence and recording uncertainty, mapping audiences and channels, drafting evidence-backed stories and policy options, and organizing lessons for reuse. You also review digital content against WCAG 2.2 (2023) and plan communication monitoring, producing draft briefs, content plans, and other work products.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who translate evidence and organizational learning into digital content, reusable knowledge, and policy advice. It suits intermediate practitioners who coordinate review, work across specialist teams, or prepare material for decision-makers.
prerequisites: Intermediate-level experience in communications, knowledge management, research communications, or policy work is expected. You should be familiar with drafting or reviewing professional content and working with evidence or stakeholder input. No coding or programming is required.
